## Arizona scope and status notes (2026-09-27)

- **Scope:** Arizona state law only. Municipal and county ordinances flagged, not resolved (instruction 20): Phoenix, Tucson, Tempe, Flagstaff and others (fair housing classes, pool ordinances, rental programs). Mobile-home parks (ch. 11) and RV spaces (ch. 19) deprioritized.
- **Settings:** Opus, high effort, ordinary search and fetch. Research mode NOT used. Primary text was read verbatim in Taylor's built-in browser from azleg.gov until his computer went offline mid-session; after that, fetches needed approvals that timed out, so the remaining reads are listed as open (AZ log §7).
- **Currency:** azleg.gov ARS pages print no history lines, and the compilation says it reflects law effective January 1 after the latest session (2026). Session laws confirmed by chapter: Laws 2023 ch. 204 (SB 1131), Laws 2025 ch. 191 (HB 2068), Laws 2025 ch. 253 (SB 1082), Laws 2026 ch. 69 (SB 1426), Laws 2026 ch. 240 (SB 1683). General effective dates (official page): 2024-09-14, 2025-09-26, 2026-09-12; no special sessions 2024-2026. Full-text scan of every 2024 (259), 2025 (265) and 2026 (264) chapter: no amendment to ch. 10 (AZ log §15.6).
- **Research-mode pass (2026-09-27, once):** settled the general effective dates, local licensing/registration and rental-tax preemption, the drug-lab repeal, the DV definition, the §33-443 amendment, the pool form and the marijuana rule; found in-force §33-1332 missing from the compilation. It did NOT run the azleg full-text search, so smoke/CO alarms, county rent control and the proof-of-absence list stay open (AZ log §12).
- **Full-text search (2026-09-27, close-out):** the official ARS search was run in Taylor's browser for the whole proof-of-absence list and the instruction-28 typography terms. Exact-phrase matching, so every term was run in variants. It FOUND a statute the research pass missed (A.R.S. §36-1637 smoke detectors) and upgraded mold, radon, EV charging, immigration, source of income, fee caps, deposit interest, rent-increase notice, carbon monoxide and dwelling servicemember rules to code-wide confirmed absences (AZ log §15).
- **Proof-of-absence (initial pass):** no code-wide searches were run then; the close-out search above superseded the ch. 10 boundary for the topics it names.
- **Instruction 19:** every row id named in the AZ cells and sections was checked against the CSV (AZ log §8).
- **New standing instruction:** 35 (compilations without history lines).

## Georgia scope and status notes (2026-09-28)

- **Scope:** Georgia state law only. Municipal and county ordinances (Atlanta, Savannah and others: rental registration, inspection, fair-housing classes, security standards under O.C.G.A. § 44-7-4) flagged, not resolved (instruction 20). Abandoned mobile homes (ch. 7 art. 6), transportable housing (§ 44-7-59), croppers and crop rent (art. 5, §§ 44-7-17, 44-7-57) deprioritized.
- **Settings:** Opus, high effort. Research mode NOT used: the proof-of-absence and outside-title work ran on the official O.C.G.A. full-text search in Taylor's built-in browser (Taylor granted 'always allow' for advance.lexis.com and law.justia.com).
- **Currency:** Justia's '2025 Code of Georgia' already prints 2026 session law (history lines cite Ga. L. 2026, pp. 278, 988, 1069) and the 2027 version of § 44-7-50. Every ch. 7 section's history line was read; 2024-2026 amendments: HB 404 (2024; §§ 44-7-13, 44-7-14.1, 44-7-30.1, 44-7-50), SB 450 (2024; § 44-7-56), HB 1203 (2024; § 44-7-55), HB 1017 (2024; squatting), HB 270 (2025; § 44-7-51), HB 399 (2025; § 44-7-25), SB 153 (2025; stylistic), HB 668 (2026; ch. 30-4), HB 1268 (2026; stylistic, incl. § 44-7-20), SB 406 (2026; § 44-7-50(e) eff. 2027-01-01). No special-session amendment appears in any history line read.
- **Instruction 19/38:** every row id named in the GA cells and sections was checked against the output CSV (GA log §8).
- **New standing instructions:** 44 (statutes that convert lease-agreed terms into landlord duties) and 45 (fetch-tool summaries can be stale; read the host page's history line).

## North Carolina scope and status notes (2026-09-28)

- **Scope:** North Carolina state law only. Municipal ordinances (Charlotte, Raleigh, Durham and others: housing codes, heat ordinances, towing, the rental registration that G.S. 160D-1207 still allows) flagged, not resolved (instruction 20). Vacation rentals under 90 days (Chapter 42A) and transient occupancies (§ 42-14.6) carved out (`edu-vacation-rental-scope-nc`). Deprioritized: manufactured home spaces and communities (§§ 42-14 proviso, 42-14.3, 42-36.1; G.S. 44A-2(e2)), agricultural tenancies (Article 2, §§ 42-7, 42-23, 42-27), lease-option contracts (Chapter 47G), rental referral agencies (G.S. 66-142 to 66-146).
- **Settings:** Opus, high effort. Research mode NOT used: the official compilation was loaded chapter by chapter in the built-in browser (Taylor granted 'always allow' for ncleg.gov) and searched with exact regular expressions, which did the proof-of-absence and cross-title work directly.
- **Currency:** ncleg.gov chapter pages print each section's history line; Chapter 42's latest are S.L. 2025-45, 2025-52 and 2025-54. Every 2025 and 2026 session law was fetched and screened for Chapter 42 and landlord-tenant terms (2025: S.L. 2025-1 to 2025-97; 2026: S.L. 2026-1 to 2026-61); only S.L. 2025-45, -52, -54 (§ 42-46), 2025-88 (squatters, G.S. 14-159.50 ff., eff. 2025-12-01) and 2026-59 s. 52 (G.S. 62-110(g), pre-1989 mobile home parks) touch the topic. § 42-46(i)(4)-(5) is garbled in the compilation (instruction 46).
- **Instruction 19/38:** every row id named in the NC cells and sections was checked against the output CSV (NC log §8).
- **New standing instructions:** 46 (read the session laws when a compiled subdivision reads oddly) and 47 (screen the state's UETA for notice exclusions).

## South Carolina scope and status notes (2026-09-28)

- **Scope:** state law only. Municipal ordinances (Charleston, Columbia, Greenville, Myrtle Beach and others) out of scope (instruction 20). Vacation rentals under 90 days (Vacation Rental Act, S.C. Code Ann. § 27-50-230) and transient accommodations (S.C. Code Ann. § 27-40-120(4)) recorded as exclusions, not researched. Manufactured home park lots (Chapter 47 of Title 27) deprioritized. All in `edu-scope-exclusions-sc`.
- **Currency:** the online Code is current through the 2025 session; 2026 Act Nos. 184, 214 and 252 change landlord-tenant law and are cited by act (instruction 50). Act No. 214 takes effect 2027-01-01 (instruction 34).
- **Decisions (Taylor, 2026-09-28):** opt-in `holdover-rate-sc` (same as GA/NC); keep the shared `default-by-tenant`; opt-in `casualty-landlord-termination-sc`; real lease is the SC REALTORS Form 410 copy uploaded in 2021 (no newer copy available).
- **Counts:** SC 110 active (69 lease clauses, 41 education), all VERIFIED; 17 confirmed-absent rows.

## Tennessee scope and status notes (2026-09-28)

- **Scope:** state law only. Municipal ordinances (Metro Nashville, Memphis, Knoxville, Chattanooga and others) out of scope (instruction 20); state statutes that reach only named or bracketed counties and cities are recorded as the county layer (instruction 51) and flagged, not resolved. Short-term rentals (Tenn. Code Ann. §§ 13-7-601 to 13-7-606) out. Transient lodging, institutional residence, contract-for-sale occupancy, condominium or co-op owners and agricultural premises are excluded from the Act (§ 66-28-102(c)).
- **County split:** URLTA (Title 66 Chapter 28) in Anderson, Blount, Bradley, Davidson, Hamilton, Knox, Madison, Maury, Montgomery, Rutherford, Sevier, Shelby, Sullivan, Sumner, Washington, Williamson and Wilson; Title 66 Chapter 7 in the other 78; Title 29 Chapter 18 (detainer), the four double-enacted rules, smoke alarms, bad checks, fair housing and rent-control preemption everywhere. Three lease pairs (`tn-urlta-late-fee`, `tn-urlta-deposit-return`, `tn-urlta-landlord-entry`); every TN row carries a `TN-SCOPE:` marker.
- **COUNTY-LAYER PILOT (Taylor, 2026-09-28):** Tennessee is the guinea pig for the future county/local layer across all states. The builder needs a property-county attribute to choose pair variants and to hide county-limited clauses (TN log Addendum M flag).
- **Currency:** Justia's host copy prints the 2025 code; every 2025 and 2026 public chapter screened in full text; 2026 Pub. Ch. 606 (firearms, effective 2027-01-01 for leases entered, amended, extended or renewed from then) and 657 (§ 29-18-136) read in enrolled text and confirmed on the LexisNexis site (instructions 34, 50).
- **Decisions (Taylor, 2026-09-28):** two versions for county-limited rules (pilot); opt-in `holdover-rate-tn` (same as GA/NC/SC); offer all three statutory landlord options as opt-ins - `eviction-service-party-tn` (statewide), `possession-bond-tn` (other counties only), `household-goods-lien-tn` (Act counties only). Real lease: TN REALTORS RF421 (2018).

## Virginia scope and status notes (2026-09-28)

- **Scope:** state law only. Local ordinances out of scope (instruction 20); the Act supersedes local landlord-tenant ordinances (Va. Code Ann. § 55.1-1201), and the local powers it leaves (inspection districts, security devices for 5+ units, smoke alarms, towing, 2026 habitability suits and affordability-expiry ordinances) are recorded in `edu-local-preemption-va`, not resolved. Excluded occupancies (§ 55.1-1201(C)-(D)): institutions, fraternal housing, condominium and co-op owners, campgrounds, rent-free occupancy, employee housing, contract-for-sale purchasers, recovery residences and transient lodging under 90 days. Manufactured home lots (Chapter 13) and nonresidential tenancies (Chapter 14) deprioritized.
- **Portfolio-size tiers (decision 1, Taylor 2026-09-28):** four `va-size-*` pairs (payment methods, redemption limit, renewal and rent-increase notice, plug-in solar), the more-than-4 variant is the default; every VA row carries a `VA-SCOPE:` marker. Cross-state Addendum M flag: per-state 'rental units owned' landlord attribute (VA log §14).
- **Currency:** the official section pages print 2026 text and delayed versions side by side; the Law Library bulk files did not, so the whole-code corpus was overlaid with the 2026 update pages (instruction 55). Every 2024, 2025 and 2026 act in the Chapter 12 history lines read in chaptered text, with effective-date clauses (2027-01-01: 2026 Acts chs. 998, 1052, 1111, 1117, 1118; 2027-07-01: chs. 640, 783, 784, 1050, 1066, 1105). 2026 Special Session I produced only the budget act (ch. 1), not searched.
- **Decisions (Taylor, 2026-09-28):** (1) two versions only where wording differs by portfolio size, as in the Tennessee county pilot; (2) offer the homestead waiver as an optional clause in the statutory words of § 34-22 (`homestead-waiver-va`). Real lease: Virginia REALTORS Form 200 (Rev. 07/23; the 07-2026 edition is members-only).

## Alabama scope and status notes (2026-09-28)

- **Scope:** state law only. The Act applies statewide with no county, city or unit-count split (Ala. Code § 35-9A-121, § 35-9A-122), so no two-version rows. Local ordinances are out of scope and largely preempted (Ala. Code § 35-9A-121; § 11-80-8.1); Class 1 vacant-property registration (Ala. Code § 11-67C-1 ff., 2026-10-01) and Birmingham, Huntsville, Mobile and Montgomery code enforcement flagged, not resolved (instruction 20). Short-term rentals out of scope; manufactured-home lots (Chapter 12A) deprioritized; agricultural rentals excluded by the Act.
- **Currency:** ALISON prints history lines and versions keyed to effective dates, including every 2026 regular-session amendment effective 2026-10-01 or later; the only 2026 special session enacted two election acts. Chapter 9A was last amended by Act 2018-473; no 2024-2026 act amended it. Act 2024-237 added the squatter chapter (Chapter 9B), third-degree burglary and the fraudulent-lease crime; Act 2026-536 turns the fraudulent-lease crime into a felony and adds an aggravated offense from 2026-10-01.
- **Decisions (Taylor, 2026-09-28):** (1) keep the library's late-fee sentence in `default-by-tenant-al`; (2) offer `holdover-rate-al` and `casualty-landlord-termination-al`; (3) offer the Birmingham `sex-offender-statement-al` clause; (4) offer the personal-property exemption waiver as an optional clause (`exemption-waiver-al`), for consistency, although Taylor dislikes it. Real lease: Alabama REALTORS Form 401 (12-11-2006), because the current RF 3.1 (revised 4/1/2026) is sold only to members and licensees.
- **Product gaps (Addendum M):** separate-document outputs for the showing notice, the scheduled-service notice and non-single-family repair agreements (instruction 57); a municipality attribute for the Birmingham rows.

## Pennsylvania scope and status notes (2026-09-29)

- **Scope:** state law only. Philadelphia and Pittsburgh ordinances (rental licensing, lead-safe certification, Philadelphia's Fair Housing Ordinance and good-cause rules, source-of-income ordinances) out of scope, flagged, not resolved (instruction 20); no statewide preemption of local landlord-tenant ordinances located. Short-term rentals out of scope; manufactured-home communities (Manufactured Home Community Rights Act, 1976 P.L. 1176, No. 261) and agricultural leases deprioritized.
- **Currency:** each official title file carries a revision stamp (2022-03-07 for the Constitution to 2026-09-16 for Title 42); every one of the 61 title-amending acts of 2024-2026 predates its title's stamp; no special-session act in 2024-2026. The 1951 Act was last amended by Act 88 of 2024. 66 Pa.C.S. Chapter 14 (utility customer protection) expired 2024-12-31. Pending: the order at 56 Pa.B. 2569 (magisterial district rules, effective 2026-11-01: Chapter 500 commentary; fee-waiver and other wording in Rules 206.1, 1002, 1008 and 1016); Act 46 of 2026 (towing, effective 2026-12-17).
- **Decisions (Taylor, 2026-09-29; PA log §6):**
  - (1) The notice-to-quit waiver is an optional clause.
  - (2) Abandoned property mirrors the statute, plus an education row on lease-set terms.
  - (3) `severability` is rewritten in plain language for all 21 tagged states: a uniform shared-text edit, with propagation notes in the AL and VA logs and, for the other 18 logs, in PA log §9 for Claude Code.
  - (4) No confession-of-judgment clause.
  - (5) The deposit cap is education, not a lease clause (instruction 65); the six other states that carry cap clauses are handed to Claude Code (PA log §9.2).
  - (A) Lead 14 is closed by 68 P.S. § 250.205.

  Real lease: Pennsylvania REALTORS® Form RL (rev. 9/17, rel. 1/18), the current edition, as completed by a Lancaster property manager and posted by Franklin & Marshall College.
- **Product gaps (Addendum M):**
  - Deposit-cap validation in the builder for every state with a cap, since caps are education rather than lease text (instruction 65; PA log §14).
  - The consumer-restrictions statement's waiver list, filled from the options chosen (instruction 61).
  - The remaining gaps: a lease readability check; a building-size attribute (three or more households) for the CO alarm and Article V-A rows; a city-class attribute for rent withholding.
